A '''semiregular space''' is a [[topological space]] whose [[regular open set]]s (sets that equal the interiors of their closures) form a [[Base (topology)|base]] for the topology.<ref name="willard"/>

==Properties and examples==

Every [[regular space]] is semiregular.<ref name="willard">{{citation|title=General Topology|first=Stephen|last=Willard|publisher=Dover|year=2004|isbn=978-0-486-43479-7|page=98|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-o8xJQ7Ag2cC&pg=PA98|contribution=14E. Semiregular spaces}}.</ref>
The converse is not true.  For example, the space <math>X = \Reals^2 \cup \{0^*\}</math> with the [[double origin topology]]<ref>Steen & Seebach, example #74</ref> and the [[Arens square]]<ref>Steen & Seebach, example #80</ref> are [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] semiregular spaces that are not regular.

Open subspaces of a semiregular space are semiregular.{{sfn|Engelking|1989|loc=Problem 2.7.6(b)}}
But arbitrary subspaces, even closed subspaces, need not be semiregular.{{sfn|Engelking|1989|loc=Problem 2.7.6(b)}}

The [[product (topology)|product]] of an arbitrary family of semiregular spaces is semiregular.{{sfn|Engelking|1989|loc=Problem 2.7.6(b)}}

Every topological space may be embedded into a semiregular space.<ref name="willard" />
